failure_or_stopping_observations: Both first candidates showed a -0.001 sampled floor gap for every wheel (SDK event 13).
Final check rounded all ten gaps to zero (event 25); this is not proof of exact contact over the full mesh or mechanical connectivity.

candidate_knowledge.problem: Chair wheels appear unsupported above reconstructed floor.
candidate_knowledge.observed_defect: Supplied teacher diagnosis reports original aggregate minimum 0.030 versus highest listed floor 0.015; student did not independently measure the original in this branch.
candidate_knowledge.cause_hypothesis: Wheel vertical extent/orientation or whole-assembly placement may explain the gap; not established uniquely.
candidate_knowledge.executed_method: Compared a fixed 0.016 whole-chair lowering against rotated cylinder casters with fork, then raised redesigned wheels 0.001.
candidate_knowledge.applicability: Potentially useful for rigid chair assemblies on a locally flat floor; cross-scene transfer untested.
candidate_knowledge.verification: Student evaluated vertices and cast local floor rays for each wheel; A and B initially -0.001, final rounded zero. Read A/B camera and side images.
candidate_knowledge.side_effects: Whole-chair lowering changes seat height; caster revision changes silhouette and connector geometry. Both first candidates penetrated sampled floor by 0.001.
candidate_knowledge.unvalidated: Sampling is not a full surface intersection or connector continuity test; true reference-space geometry and clearance remain unknown.

limitations: No hidden reference geometry is available; reference silhouette judgments are image-based.

Evaluator scene states and target_geometry.json are independent outputs, not student checks. target_geometry.json:2528-2550 independently records a final caster bottom near 0.015 and a fork, consistent with final code; it does not establish mechanical connectivity.
The student-generated contact_check.py is a scene-specific check, not a general reusable skill snippet. It imports BVHTree but does not use it for mesh-distance calculations.
Floor height is the maximum ray hit over near-lowest sampled wheel vertices, so it does not certify every point against floor penetration or support.
No evidence of a full-reference image plane replacing reconstruction; final source constructs geometry and constant materials.
